question.text: How many additional US states will enact bans on cultivated meat before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves as the number of additional US states which enact a law prohibiting the sale of cultivated meat before July 1, 2027.

The following states will not be considered for this question:

* Alabama
* Florida 
* Indiana
* Mississippi
* Montana
* Nebraska
* South Dakota
* Texas 

If no new prohibitions on the sale of cultivated meat become law in any additional US state before July 1, 2027, this question resolves as **Zero**.

## Cultivated meat bans: research brief (as of 2026-11-19)

As far as I can find, no state outside the excluded list has enacted a full ban on selling cultivated meat. Every serious 2026 bill in a non-excluded state died. The question will be decided almost entirely by the 2027 legislative sessions, which mostly run January to June 2027.

### 1. Resolution source
- There is no single official data series. The best tracker is the National Agricultural Law Center's state compilation. Its last update was 2026-04-07. It lists sale bans in AL, FL, IN (until 2027-06-30), MS, MT, NE and TX (until 2027-09-01). Louisiana's ban only takes effect after a US Supreme Court ruling. Tennessee has a permit system, not a ban. GA, OK, SC, WV, ID and VA have labeling laws only. [NALC](https://nationalaglawcenter.org/state-compilations/alternative-protein-laws-state-compilation/)
- 2026-10-26: A secondary tracker lists the same 8 states (all excluded) and says Louisiana's trigger has not been met. It names no other new ban states. Arizona's HB 2762, signed 2026-06-19, is a labeling law. [tallow.app](https://tallow.app/blog/lab-grown-meat-bans-eight-states-which-expire-what-fda-cleared)

### 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that settles the question. The count is currently 0. I found no enacted ban in a non-excluded state from April 2026 to November 2026.
- 2026-02-24: South Carolina's H.5096 passed the House 110-0 on 2026-02-19, but it never got past the Senate Agriculture Committee (last action 2026-02-24). The 2025-26 session has ended, so the bill is dead. [SC Legislature](https://www.scstatehouse.gov/billsearch.php?billnumbers=hb5096)
- 2026-04-15: Kentucky's HB 309 passed committee on 2026-02-04, then was sent back to House Appropriations & Revenue on 2026-04-15, per a tracker. It is dead. [LPM](https://www.lpm.org/news/2026-02-04/republicans-seek-to-ban-lab-grown-meat-before-it-hits-kentucky-shelves), [KY record](https://apps.legislature.ky.gov/record/26RS/hb309.html)
- 2026: In Georgia, SB 415 was referred to committee on 2026-01-27 with no votes recorded. HB 201 is listed as dead as of 2026-04-02. [legiplex](https://app.azure.legiplex.com/ga/legislature/2025/2025-r/bills/sb415)
- 2026: In West Virginia, HB 4462 died in committee. SB 932 got no action after its 2026-02-12 committee referral. [WV Legislature](https://bills.wvlegislature.gov/bill/history/2026/RS/SB932)
- 2026-02-11: Oklahoma's SB 2121 was placed on the Senate General Order calendar. I found no floor vote and could not confirm its final status. Oklahoma's 2025 law is described as labeling, not a ban. [OK billsum](https://www.oklegislature.gov/cf_pdf/2025-26%20SUPPORT%20DOCUMENTS/BILLSUM/Senate/SB2121%20INT%20BILLSUM.PDF)
- 2026-03-27: Wisconsin's governor vetoed AB 554, a labeling bill with some sales restrictions. [CSG Midwest](https://csgmidwest.org/2026/05/04/though-not-yet-on-grocery-shelves-lab-grown-meat-is-focus-of-new-laws-and-legislation/)

### 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-18: Experts debunked viral claims that cultivated meat is being secretly sold in grocery stores. [Women's Health](https://www.womenshealthmag.com/health/a74456527/lab-grown-meat/)
- 2026-08-13: Pennsylvania's SB 1422 and HB 2139, which would ban sales, are both stuck in committee. Pennsylvania has a Democratic governor. [Altoona Mirror](https://www.altoonamirror.com/news/local-news/2026/08/pa-generalassembly-meat-lab-grown-bills-target/)
- 2026-03-23: An 11th Circuit panel upheld Florida's ban. [Florida Phoenix](https://floridaphoenix.com/2026/03/23/federal-appellate-panel-upholds-floridas-ban-on-lab-grown-meat/)
- 2026-03-12: South Dakota's governor signed a five-year moratorium (SB 124), after vetoing a permanent ban (HB 1077). This shows a pattern of governors choosing moratoria over permanent bans. [SD Searchlight](https://southdakotasearchlight.com/2026/03/11/governor-signs-lab-grown-meat-moratorium-property-protections-crypto-national-security-bills/)
- 2026-01: In Texas, a judge denied the state's motion to dismiss the Upside/Wildtype lawsuit (a dormant Commerce Clause claim) but also denied an injunction. [Green Queen](https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/judge-deals-early-blow-to-texas-in-lawsuit-over-cultivated-meat-ban/)
- 2026-01-20: Arizona introduced HB 2791, a ban. The state enacted a labeling law (HB 2762) instead. [AZ Capitol Times](https://azcapitoltimes.com/news/2026/01/20/arizona-may-become-first-state-to-ban-lab-grown-meat/)

### 4. Base rates (new states enacting full sale bans per year)
- 2024: 2 (FL in May, AL in May).
- 2025: 5 (MS, MT, IN, NE, TX). This was the peak.
- 2026: 1 (SD, a moratorium). Every bill in a non-excluded state failed, including bills that passed one chamber in SC and committee in KY.
- Trend: a sharp drop after 2025. Most of the easiest Republican-controlled states have already acted. Remaining Republican-led states (GA, OK, SC, KY, WV) have repeatedly chosen labeling laws instead. Most enactments are signed between March and June, which falls inside this question's window.

### 5. Other forecasts
- The Kalshi market "Which states will ban lab-grown meat? (Before 2026)" has expired and covers the wrong period: TN, AZ and NH all trade at 0.01. I found no Kalshi or Polymarket market for 2027.
- Manifold, "How many states will ban... by end of 2028": expected value 5, with only 7 holders and 11 trades. It looks stale, since 8 states already have bans. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Noah1/how-many-states-will-ban-the-sale-o)
- Metaculus: I found nothing relevant.

### 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- January to June 2027: most legislatures meet. Watch for reintroduced bills in GA, OK, SC, WV, KY, PA, MI and IL, and in states with Republican control and no current law (e.g. TN, MO, ID, WY, ND, AR, OH, IA, KS, UT).
- Results of the November 2026 governor races could change veto risk in some states. I did not research these.
- Indiana's moratorium expires 2027-06-30 and Texas's ban 2027-09-01. Both states are excluded, but debates over renewing them may encourage other states to copy them.
- The Texas lawsuit and any further appeal in the Florida case could affect whether legislators think bans will survive in court. A Supreme Court ruling would also be needed to switch on Louisiana's trigger law, and that is very unlikely before July 2027.
- I found no prefiled bills for 2027 yet.

Caveats: the NALC tracker has not been updated since April 2026, and I could not confirm Oklahoma SB 2121's final status directly.

# Cultivated meat sale bans: research for the question "additional US states before July 2027"

**Bottom line:** I found no new state that has fully banned cultivated meat sales since the April 2026 list. The count still stands at **0** as of 2026-11-19. Louisiana passed a ban in 2026, but it only takes effect after a US Supreme Court ruling, so it does not count yet.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question has no single data series. It turns on state statutes signed into law. Trackers I used: the National Agricultural Law Center (NALC), CSG Midwest and LifeMate.
- 2026-08-15: LifeMate lists exactly eight states with sale bans, the same eight the question excludes. South Dakota's SB 124, signed 2026-03-12, is the newest. [LifeMate](https://lifematetech.com/articles/cultivated-meat-federal-clearance-state-bans)
- Undated 2026 report: NALC's Stone says 8 states restrict the sale or manufacture of cultivated meat, and 23 have labeling laws. [RFD-TV](https://www.rfdtv.com/alternative-protein-laws-keep-changing-across-farm-states?p=175)

## 2. Current status
- **Louisiana (trigger law, does not count yet):** HB 512 was signed 2026-05-29 as Act 555, and SB 152 was also enacted. Both bans take effect only after a final US Supreme Court ruling that such bans are constitutional. [LA Legislature](https://legis.la.gov/Legis/BillInfo.aspx?i=250338), [NALC](https://nationalaglawcenter.org/food-law-in-the-states-2026-update-part-2/)
- **Possible path through the courts:** On 2026-03-23 the 11th Circuit upheld the denial of a preliminary injunction against Florida's ban. I found no report that Upside Foods has asked the Supreme Court to hear the case. If the Court did rule for the states before July 2027, Louisiana's law would kick in. That looks unlikely in the time left, but I could not confirm the docket. [Duane Morris](https://blogs.duanemorris.com/animallawdevelopments/2026/03/25/lab-grown-meat-meets-the-supremacy-clause-11th-circuit-weighs-in-on-federal-pre-emption/)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-06-19: Arizona's HB 2762 was signed. It only requires labels, so it does not count. [NALC/RFD-TV](https://www.rfdtv.com/alternative-protein-laws-keep-changing-across-farm-states?p=175)
- 2026-03-30: South Dakota failed to override the veto of HB 1077, a permanent ban. The temporary 2026-2031 ban (SB 124) stands. [SD Searchlight](https://southdakotasearchlight.com/2026/03/30/lawmakers-fail-to-override-vetoes-of-lab-grown-meat-ban-and-in-home-care-regulations/)
- 2026-03-27: Wisconsin Gov. Evers vetoed AB 554, a labeling bill that also banned serving cultivated meat in schools. It was not a sale ban. [CSG Midwest](https://csgmidwest.org/2026/05/04/though-not-yet-on-grocery-shelves-lab-grown-meat-is-focus-of-new-laws-and-legislation/)
- 2026-02-24: South Carolina's H.5096, a full ban, passed the House 110-0 on 2026-02-19 and was sent to the Senate Agriculture Committee on 2026-02-24. It got no further action, so it died when the 2025-26 session ended. [SC Statehouse](https://www.scstatehouse.gov/billsearch.php?billnumbers=5096&session=126&summary=B)
- 2026-02-03: Oklahoma's SB 2116 was referred to the Agriculture and Wildlife committee and shows no later action. SB 2121 is listed as dead. In 2025 the House had passed HB 2829 by 72-18, but it died in the Senate. [OK Legislature](http://www.oklegislature.gov/BillInfo.aspx?Bill=SB2116&Session=2600)
- Early 2026, Georgia: SB 415 stalled in Senate committee after 2026-01-27, and HB 201 was listed as dead by 2026-04-02. [BillTrack50](https://www.billtrack50.com/billdetail/1812498)
- Early 2026, West Virginia: SB 225, SB 932 and HB 4462 all stalled, and nothing was enacted. [WV Legislature](https://bills.wvlegislature.gov/bill/history/2026/RS/HB4462)
- 2026-02-23, Wyoming: HB 61 was not considered by the full House. [WY Leg](https://www.wyoleg.gov/Legislation/2026/HB0061)
- 2026-05-04: Bills in Illinois (HB 15) and Michigan (HB 4083) have been stuck in committee since 2025. [CSG Midwest](https://csgmidwest.org/2026/05/04/though-not-yet-on-grocery-shelves-lab-grown-meat-is-focus-of-new-laws-and-legislation/)
- I found no bills prefiled for 2027 and no lawmakers announcing 2027 bans.

## 4. Base rates (new full sale bans signed)
- 2024: 2 states (Florida, Alabama).
- 2025: 5 states (Mississippi, Montana, Indiana, Nebraska, Texas). 2025 was an odd year, when many legislatures hold long sessions.
- 2026: 1 state (South Dakota), plus Louisiana's trigger law.
- 18 states introduced 30 bills in one year, so most bills fail. [NCSL](https://www.ncsl.org/resources/details/will-states-take-lab-grown-meat-off-the-table)
- The window to resolution covers almost all of the 2027 sessions, which run roughly January to June. 2027, like 2025, is the first year of new two-year sessions in many states. Pressure from the ranching lobby continues, and in 2026 the 11th Circuit sided with Florida's ban.
- Governors have pushed back: the Wisconsin and South Dakota vetoes, and Tennessee shelving its bill on consumer-choice grounds.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi "Which states will ban lab-grown meat?" (KXCMEATBAN): the 2025 contracts settled No. Tennessee, Arizona and New Hampshire were at about 1%. I found no 2027 version of this market. [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxcmeatban)
- I found nothing matching on Polymarket, Metaculus or Manifold. The Manifold market on states banning animal meat by 2050 (31%) is a different question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **2027 sessions start in January.** States to watch:
  - South Carolina could reintroduce its ban after the 110-0 House vote.
  - Oklahoma has passed a ban through the House before.
  - Georgia, West Virginia, Wyoming, Tennessee, Kentucky, Arkansas, Missouri, Idaho, Utah and North Dakota also have 2027 sessions. North Dakota stripped a ban from a bill in 2025.
  - Most of these sessions end between March and May. Louisiana's runs into June.
- **Texas and Indiana:** Texas's ban expires 2027-09-01 and Indiana's on 2027-06-30. Extending them would not count because both states are excluded, but those fights could spread model bills to other states.
- **Supreme Court:** any petition from the Florida (Upside) case or the Texas litigation would matter for Louisiana's trigger.
- **Possible brakes:** if Upside, Wildtype or other companies start meaningful retail sales, new bans could gain urgency or meet more resistance. Further vetoes are also possible.

(a) **Time left:** About 7.5 months, until 2027-07-01. Almost all the relevant action happens in the January to June 2027 legislative sessions. Most sale bans in earlier years were signed between March and June, inside this window.

(b) **Status quo:** No non-excluded state has enacted a full sale ban as of 2026-11-19, so the status quo answer is 0. No 2027 bills have been prefiled yet.

(c) **Base rates:** New states enacting sale bans or moratoria, by calendar year:
- 2024: 2 (Florida, Alabama).
- 2025: 5 (Mississippi, Montana, Indiana, Nebraska, Texas), the peak.
- 2026: 1 (South Dakota, a moratorium).

Over a comparable window of about half a year (one session season), outcomes have ranged from 1 to 5. The pool of easy Republican-trifecta states is shrinking, though. Several remaining Republican-led states (Georgia, Oklahoma, South Carolina, West Virginia, Idaho, Arizona) have chosen labeling laws instead of bans. Odd-year sessions are longer and more numerous, and some states such as North Dakota meet only in odd years. That modestly favors more action in 2027 than in 2026.

(d) **Strongest evidence:**
- **South Carolina:** H.5096 passed the House 110-0 on 2026-02-19 but stalled in the Senate Agriculture Committee and is now dead. It is a plausible candidate if reintroduced in the 2027-28 session.
- **Kentucky:** HB 309 cleared committee on 2026-02-04, then died on 2026-04-15.
- **Georgia and West Virginia:** Bills died in committee in 2026.
- **Oklahoma:** SB 2121's status is unclear but it likely died.
- **Arizona:** The state chose a labeling law (HB 2762, signed 2026-06-19) over the HB 2791 ban.
- **Wisconsin:** The governor vetoed a restriction bill (2026-03-27).
- **Pennsylvania:** Ban bills are stuck in committee, and the governor is a Democrat.
- **South Dakota:** The governor vetoed a permanent ban but signed a moratorium (2026-03-12), so a moratorium path exists and counts.
- **Courts:** The 11th Circuit upheld Florida's ban (2026-03-23), which reduces legal-risk concerns for legislators. The Texas Commerce Clause suit survived dismissal, which cuts the other way.
- **Markets:** No liquid market covers this question.

(e) **Unexpected scenario:** Florida's appellate win, plus renewal debates in Indiana and Texas, could revive momentum. South Carolina, Kentucky, North Dakota and Arkansas might each pass bans or moratoria in spring 2027, giving 3 or more. Alternatively, a court loss for Texas could chill everything and leave the count at 0.

**Adjustment:** I start from a base rate of roughly 1 to 2 per session season. I shift toward 0 because of the 2026 pattern: every non-excluded bill failed and states kept preferring labeling laws. I partially offset that because odd-year sessions are larger and South Carolina came close.
